The findings below are the places the SSO callback bypasses that contract.

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:331-340 — the SSO callback upsert_sso_user() map_err returns (INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, Json(SsoError::new("user_create_failed", &e.to_string()))): the raw user-service/DB (sqlx) error string is serialized into the public JSON response body.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:343-352 — same pattern for create_session(): Json(SsoError::new("session_create_failed", &e.to_string())) leaks the raw session/redis/infra error to the internet-facing caller.

This directly violates the public-surface error contract documented in backend/servers/reality-server/src/util/errors.rs:1-32, which states reality-server is internet-facing and raw sqlx/anyhow error strings can leak column names, constraint names, and pool/TLS state; util::errors::db_error exists precisely to scrub these at the map_err boundary. The sibling inquiries route already routes DatabaseError through db_error (routes/inquiries.rs:173) and the registration route logs-then-returns a generic body (routes/users.rs:220-226); the SSO callback is the inconsistent outlier.

Fix: log server-side via tracing::error!(error = %e, ...) and return a fixed generic message (mirror RegistrationResult::DatabaseError handling / util::errors::db_error). No existing open backlog finding covers reality-server SSO callback error leakage.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:310-318 — exchange_code_for_tokens() map_err returns Json(SsoError::new("token_exchange_failed", &e.to_string())), echoing the raw upstream PM OAuth HTTP/reqwest error (can carry the internal PM token endpoint URL / transport detail) to the public client.

Lower severity than the DB/infra leak (upstream HTTP error text is less sensitive than sqlx constraint/connection detail), but same class and same remediation: log server-side, return a generic stable code only. Keeping all four callback branches (token_exchange/user_info/user_create/session_create) consistent with util::errors would close the whole info-disclosure surface on the SSO callback.
